# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A)

## BOOK 1 of 2: A LITTLE IRISH GIRL (J. M. Callwell; Blackie & Son)

**Chapter list:** I Miss Clarksons' Educational Establishment; II Cousin Ansey's Legacy; III Norah's Freak; IV Within Sound of the Sea; V English Ideas and Irish Ways; VI Cousins; VII Moyross Abbey; VIII Ballintaggart Cave; IX The Ghost in the Monk's Walk; X Captain Lester, R.M.; XI On Drinane Head; XII Discomfited; XIII Malachy's Oration; XIV Mr. O'Brien Sees a Vision of the Past; XV It Was All Norah's Idea; XVI Peace and Harmony.

**Setting/people (London start):** Treherne House, north London school for young ladies run by Miss Clarksons (eldest Miss Clarkson, stately, sanctum on landing; Miss Susan; Miss Euphemia, youngest, teaches juniors, high white cap, strict but kindly). Fräulein Glock, German governess. Girls: Lily Allardyce (pink/fair, rich, only child, parents in Hampshire/Heron's Court, going to Paris at Easter); Louisa (flaxen, drawling); Constance Lane; big girl neighbour who nudged Norah.
- **Norah O'Brien**, 11, small, short black hair "like pony's mane", turned-up nose, wide mouth, dark-blue "Irish eyes", quick temper/mood, ringleader of pranks. Black mourning frock, frayed crape cuffs. Proud of Irish name (no h dropped... she dislikes spelling without the h).
- Father **Piers O'Brien**, journalist, genial, Irish accent, died ~6 months before after chill from coming out in wet night; Hampstead Heath home.
- Mother **Marion Belthorpe**, died long before Norah's memory; eloped with Piers the day before wedding to Uncle Nicholas.
- Siblings: **Roderick** (eldest, ~21, college honours, gave up bar, lawyer's clerk, cough, weak lungs; later writes articles for magazines, e.g. *Piccadilly*); **Anstace** (2 yrs younger than Roderick, gentle, governess to Dr. Trafford's family, mother-figure, kept diary-like practicality); **Manus** (7 yrs gap, age 12, at cheap school in Kent run by Dr. and Mrs. Ford; schoolboy writing; close to Norah; later goes to Harrow).
- **Cousin Ansey** (Anstace O'Brien, godmother of Anstace, father's relation), died at Kilshane asylum in Dublin after 12 yrs; waited for fiancé **Hugh Masters** (went to America). Left Kilshane (~£100/yr, two miles from Moyross) to the O'Briens if Hugh not heard of. Servant Biddy (Hogan), brother **Tom Hogan** (ex-coachman; gardener/steward).
- **Uncle Nicholas O'Brien** of Moyross Abbey (father's half-brother, old, grey, grim, copper mine owner, Drinane Head). Nephew/niece: **Harry Wyndham** (grandnephew, hot-headed) and **Ella Wyndham** (gentle, dreamy, ~17). Their grandmother Jess O'Brien. Governess-companion **Miss Browne** ("Brownie"), English, prejudiced, took the children from India after mother (Mrs. Wyndham) died of cholera; father Captain Wyndham also died there.
- **Mr. Lynch** (old rector, Kilshane's church on cliff) and **Mrs. Lynch**, friends; **Lady Louisa Butler** of Dromore (14 miles away).
- Kilshane: small house on cliff edge, overgrown, hens in kitchen; kitchen served by Biddy; Biddy's brood, cat, one-eyed collie. Orphans of Hogans: **Lanty** (red-headed, 7 children' eldest, poacher/mischief, later keeper), **Bride** (maid), **Kat** (2-yr-old baby). Connor (driver, outside car). Thady, Mrs. Connor (potato scones, sow eating piglets).
- Moyross: Monks' Walk glen down to cove; ruins of abbey; iron pier; copper mine; manager **M'Bain** (Scot, new machinery, brought Scotchmen). **Malachy Flanagan** (red-bearded steersman; leads still; oratorical; Norah's protector).
- Ballintaggart Cave (seal hunt with Manus, Lanty, Norah; Lanty clubs seal; seal's head kept on roof at Kilshane). Drinane Head (illicit potheen still with tarn, Lanty & Malachy's gang).
- **Captain Lester, R.M.** (resident magistrate, sandy/red-faced, jolly, stays at Kilshane; raid on still). Constable/police.

**Key events in order:**
1. Norah sent to bottom of class for daydreaming ("Tuesday fortnight"). Lily consoles her. Lily's Paris trip revealed; Norah loses holiday with Lily.
2. Anstace visits; announces fortune: Cousin Ansey's legacy; Kilshane. Norah sobs then whoops; Anstace reveals Roderick's cough; plans to live there.
3. Norah's "toboggan" freak on tea-tray down stairs with Lily; Miss Clarkson catches them; Lily hurt (sticking plaster); Norah's bumped head; Miss Clarkson kisses Norah; no punishment.
4. Journey: Dublin, Ballyfin station, outside car in rain; Tom ("Begorra" welcome), Biddy with torch of turf.
5. Kitchen chaos (hens, dog licking frying pan, Biddy hurls candlestick). Anstace disgusted; "English ideas."
6. Visiting Connor's family; Roderick's rescue of Ella's runaway pony **Sheila** at gate; Ella meets Roderick, Anstace, Norah, Manus; Miss Browne arrives with bonnet on back.
7. Ella visits Moyross; Uncle Nicholas asks about Kilshane visitors; portrait of Marion ("the one woman he loved").
8. Ballintaggart seal hunt with Lanty; Norah hides; Manus wounded (sleeve torn); seal head taken.
9. Monks' Walk "ghost" = Manus fires at table-cloth (laundry maid's cloth) Miss Browne scolds maid; Norah & Manus keep secret.
10. Still seized; Captain Lester's raid at dawn; Norah warns Lanty on Drinane Head (walks out; Malachy carries her on back, shawl disguise; Roderick sees her but doesn't recognise her).
11. Miners' rally at mine led by Malachy urging march on Moyross; Norah & Manus run to warn; Norah sets up candle + white quilt in abbey window ("ghost"); mob flees; Norah falls and is concussed; Uncle Nicholas, back early, appears; Piers' childhood memory.
12. Norah unconscious; Roderick and Anstace arrive at dawn; Uncle Nicholas reconciles ("Marion!").
13. Recovery: Harry to Army (red coat); Roderick to be heir; Roderick and Ella engaged (Monk's Walk); Miss Browne leaves; Malachy weeps; Lanty promises no potheen, becomes under-keeper (Pat Lannigan retiring); Norah tells all about table-cloth; Nicholas: "Nothing would have induced me to leave an acre of O'Brien land away from the rightful heir." Last line Anstace: "It will be a year next week since he died."

Also: Mr. M'Bain returns to Scotland; mine peace; Manus to Harrow; Anstace & Norah to live at Moyross.

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: POPPY OTT'S PEDIGREED PICKLES (Leo Edwards; Grosset & Dunlap, 1927)

**Narrator:** Jerry Todd (first person), chum **Poppy Ott** (long-legged, long-headed, schemer; father Mr. Ott, recently reformed tramp who runs stilt factory; mother dead). Town: **Tutter** (La Salle County, Illinois). Newspaper: *Tutter Daily Globe* (editor Mr. Stair). Town marshal **Bill Hadley**. Doctor **Doc Leland** (nose glasses, Lizzie car). Banker **Thomas Lorring** (Commercial Bank; backed the stilt factory; "Mr. Lorring"). Mother and Dad (Jerry's parents). Henny (Poppy's cousin in Rockford; works at Wiggins & Wakefield wholesale).

**Rivals:** **Mr. Foreman Pennykorn** (Canners Exchange Bank, owns Tutter Canning Co.; tight-fisted, grasping, "old skin-flint"); his son **Norman Pennykorn** (runs canning factory); grandson **Forrest Pennykorn** (snob, sporty roadster, "smarty", "monkey-face" taunts). Ashton Canning Co. competitor. Their brand "Dandy Dills".

**Other characters:** **Mr. Simon Weckler** (old widower, stooped, cane, housekeeper **Mrs. Clayton**; cat **Peter**, yellow, dies strangled; daughter **Clara** eloped with Nathan Weir, lost; "silent partner" of Pickle Parlor); **Butch McGinty** (bachelor "towing" and house-mover, mule **Jerusalem**, Zulutown, dirty; secret pickle recipe; wages $3.50/day; burns cookies; wears butcher apron/cap); **Mrs. Cora O'Mally** (Irish widow, cucumber farmer, lives in old **Weir house** in river bottoms; big straw hat; cellar; secret pickle recipe; widow who marries Uncle Abner); **Mrs. Bagley**, **Mrs. Brown**, **Mrs. Morgan**, **Mrs. Hempline**, **Mrs. Cook**, **Mrs. Hiram Springer**, Mrs. Bowman; **Bid Stricker**, **Red Meyers**, **Denny Kirk**, **Spider Whickleberry** (boy who rigged the cat-strangling machine); **Silas Hartenbower** (102-yr-old, told of pirate's cucumber patch and lead mold).
- Pirate: **Peg-leg Weir** (river pirate, built stone house; shot by posse; drowning/peg-leg tale).
- Uncle **Abner Weir** ("Uncle Ab", Rimtown, Ohio; old, whiskers, nightgown, Bible, talking machine) and nephew **Tommy Weir** (Tom; son of Nathan Weir; grandson of Mr. Weckler).
- **Nathan Weir**: Tom's father; one-armed; in Ohio penitentiary; jewel robbery in Peoria accomplice; "one-armed cat killer"; died in hospital.
- Deacon **Pillpopper** (boat livery, from earlier book), Captain Tinkertop (boat owner).
- Wholesalers: Wiggins & Wakefield (Rockford); Mr. Samson (food buyer for railroad); Mr. Lorrimer (railroad president).

**Key events in order:**
1. Poppy proposes "Pickle Parlor"; Jerry skeptical; they overhear Pennykorns discussing corn price, pickles (Dandy Dills), Ashton plant; Forrest snubs them; cashier says empty store rents $125/month. Poppy's pickle oration in bank.
2. Jerry spills Mrs. Clayton's pickles at Parker grocery sale; Poppy's "Providence" speech. Poppy has a jar of pickles bought at Presbyterian missionary food sale in Drake's store; maker unknown.
3. Mr. Weckler (cat Peter fished from cistern by Poppy) offers old summerhouse playhouse; "silent partner"; pay in pickles. Plan to move it to lot across from canning factory (rent $5/month to Weckler).
4. Jerry's cucumber-in-cistern pun; sign planning; store 6 ft x 8 ft; $50 each into bank account ($100, Thomas Lorring).
5. Ad "WHOSE PICKLES" in *Tutter Daily Globe* — typesetter error inserted "Seven diamonds worth ten thousand dollars." 63 letters; women visit; Mrs. Morgan; Mrs. Hempline; woman swats Jerry with broom; Jerry's sick headache: Dr. Jekyll; telegram from Peoria police chief re diamonds (Bill Hadley handles).
6. Jerry ill (pickles); Doc Leland. Burglar ransacks Poppy's cellar, dumps pickle jars (no diamonds).
7. Butch McGinty found to be pickle genius (ate 7 pickles; he gave 6 quarts to church people). Poppy hires Butch at $3.50/day (checks rejected; cash).
8. "Aunt Jemima" scheme (name for pickle brand, like pancake flour).
9. At O'Mally farm: cistern-like strange sounds in cellar; Mrs. O'Mally scared; Jerry's pirate tale (Peg-leg Weir, cucumber patch, secret tunnel, gold).
10. Swim/raft at river; Jerry in barrel mock; Pennykorn truck driver (Smarty/Forrest) argues with Mrs. O'Mally over 4 bushels; Poppy buys 4 bushels ($2/bushel).
11. Pickling at Poppy's house; Butch in apron/cap; samples 300 bottles; handbill "AUNT JEMIMA'S PICKLES"; Mr. Ott's nephew's wedding in Rockford; telegram.
12. Ptomaine poisoning at church supper (Mrs. Bowman? no — people sick; Mrs. Higgins); Jerry's pickles blamed by town/Pennykorns; Bill says poisoning actually from stuffed olives at church supper.
13. Store moved to Weckler lot; Pennykorns demand lot; Weckler refuses.
14. Weckler attacked with head wound; cat Peter strangled and tail cut; Mrs. Clayton finds him. Jerry & Poppy find gold cucumber (cast lead/gold, one-armed handprint in flower bed, wire).
15. Sunday School: "Love Lifted Me"; cat strangled through church basement window by tongs; Jerry screeches.
16. Poppy's order from Rockford (two 30-gallon barrels) and telegram to Mrs. O'Mally to buy entire crop (~700 bushels at $2). Mrs. O'Mally has 130 bushels already.
17. Pennykorn offers 90¢ for crop ("tiers" 1.00/.90/.70); Mrs. O'Mally refuses; threats ("I'll sue"; "until tomorrow noon"); Jerry calls Pennykorn "old chip of the old blockhead".
18. Underground: tunnel via creek; cement tunnel; Mrs. O'Mally; Tom.
19. Midnight: Poppy into cellar; tail cut from cat in chimney secret door; Tom captured, knocked out; Jerry gets rowboat from Deacon Pillpopper; trap; Uncle Abner & Tom reconciled with Poppy and Jerry.
20. Pickle production through church ladies (Methodist, Presbyterian, Catholic); 20 women; kegs (ten-gallon); Chicago orders; Pennykorn letter to Wiggins & Wakefield attacking "pedigreed pickles" as poisoning.
21. Strange farmer dumps cucumbers; Pennykorn offers to buy stock & pay $200 bonus; trap at bank (locked door; Bill Hadley at window); Poppy reveals he sold all stock in Chicago (six 10-gal kegs railroad, Mr. Lorrimer's dining car).
22. Gold cucumber in two halves (gold rivets); clock-face/moon/chimney/coffin sketch; dig in chimney's shadow at midnight; iron chest found; ~$35,000 treasure; each share ~$7,000 (Poppy & Jerry each $7,000 in Lorring bank).
23. Pennykorn family joins canning co. deal: new Pedigreed Pickles company $100,000 capital; 50 shares each to boys and Mrs. O'Mally; Chamber of Commerce banquet; Poppy speech (never said a word); Tom reunited with grandfather Weckler; Uncle Abner & Mrs. O'Mally marry; Butch leaves. Next book: POPPY OTT AND THE FRECKLED GOLDFISH.
